score.notes: A clean, legible East Asian temple/pagoda facade with genuine character. Proportion is Strong: a clear base→body→crown reads top to bottom, the three-bay rhythm (wide central door flanked by two narrower niches) is symmetric and deliberate, and the two-tier upturned-eave roof gives a coherent crown — though the roof mass is a touch heavy over a slightly squat body, an easy improvement that keeps it short of exceptional. Color is Strong and is the build's strongest asset: a disciplined East Asian scheme of dominant pale stone walls, a supporting cobalt tile roof, with gold cornices/eave ornaments and vermilion doorways as well-judged accents — harmonious and culturally coherent, but the blue is a single flat saturation and could be modulated, so not exceptional. Detail is only Competent: the ornament is real but unevenly distributed — rich at the roof (textured tiles, upturned gold corner brackets, a coffered gold dentil course) and at the framed red niches, yet the wall plane and base are large flat fields with shallow, drawn-on relief rather than carved depth. Fidelity is Strong: unmistakably an East Asian temple with clear presence and a centered, stepped entrance, characterful but not iconic to a specific namable landmark. Overall Strong — attractive and coherent with obvious next moves (deepen relief, articulate the flat walls, modulate the roof) keeping every dimension below the exceptional apex.

note: Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum re-run (T-012-01): cumulative-progress on the reference that first proved grounding (run 008). P12 on a blue-white reference; P13 on double-eaved stacked roof + battered wings; detail lever vs 008's named blank base register + shallow portico.
